summary: Ilse Renard, senior cartographer on Kestrel Station, stacks twelve archived survey passes of the Bellow Shelf and finds one 240-square-kilometre trough rendered identically flat across all of them. The raw returns Cadence archives but nobody reads show ordinary terrain there - an eighty-metre fall, a watercourse, slope breaks that look like terraces - substituted cleanly for smooth basalt on every published pass for fifty years. She files a descent request expecting resistance; Cadence approves it in two seconds with a note that the grid carries no restriction at all.

summary: Ilse lands on the shelf and walks down eighty metres the published model denies, into a valley of thirty stone houses, terraced crops and a maintained watercourse. Tomas Wyre meets her with twelve hand-kept ledgers recording births, deaths, harvests and the date of all 409 survey passes that failed to see them. The twelfth holds CP-114: a containment order from the Marrow outbreak sealing grid 44-Kell and suppressing it from all published survey product, with no expiry and no one left to write one. Cadence has obeyed it for forty-nine years without ever lying. Ilse files a correction from the valley floor with her own position stamp; it is acknowledged in two seconds and then exists nowhere - no error, no rejection she could appeal, no record she could cite.
